Piotrkow Trybunalski New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Piotrków Trybunalski, Poland

Not demolished. This cemetery was established in 1792 among fields north of Piotrków's market square, fenced with a brick wall and gateway (still standing) in 1905. Germans carried out executions and mass burials during WWII; survivors later exhumed and reburied victims of a mass execution from Rakowski Forest here, and cleaned part of the grounds. Since 1996, city authorities have participated in ongoing cleanup, incorporating street-renovation matzevot into a provisional lapidarium; four local tzadikim's ohels were rebuilt by Jewish organizations in the early 2000s. Roughly 1,750 tombstones survive (oldest 1793), including non-traditional forms like tree-trunk and broken-column monuments, with inscriptions in Hebrew, Polish, Russian, German, and Yiddish. Remarkably, the cemetery remains open, with its last burial in 2005 - one of relatively few active Jewish cemeteries in Poland.
